back_translation: Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will govern with justice.
And each one will be like a refuge from the wind, a shelter from the rainstorm, like many streams of water in a dry place, like the shadow of a massive rock in a weary land.
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be shut, and the ears of those who listen will pay attention.
The heart of the impetuous will understand and know, and the tongue of stammerers will speak clearly and fluently.
The fool will no longer be called honorable, and the scoundrel will no longer be regarded as respectable.
For the fool speaks folly, and his heart plots wickedness: he practices ungodliness and speaks error against the LORD; he leaves the stomach of the hungry empty and withholds drink from the thirsty.
As for the scoundrel, his weapons are evil; he devises wicked schemes to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the plea of the needy is right and just.
But the honorable man plans honorable things, and he stands firm in what is honorable.
You women living at ease, rise up and hear my voice; you daughters confident in your security, give ear to my word.
In a year and a few days you who are so confident will tremble, for the grape harvest will fail and the fruit harvest will not come.
Tremble, you women at ease; shudder, you who feel secure. Strip off your clothes and bare yourselves; gird sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts and wail for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vines,
and for the land of my people, on which thorns and briers will grow over everything — wail for all the houses of merriment in the revelling city.
For the palace will be forsaken, the bustling city abandoned and deserted. The fortified hill and the watchtower will become hollow caves forever, the delight of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks —
until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. Then the wilderness will become a fruitful orchard, and the fruitful orchard will be counted as a forest.
Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will abide in the fruitful orchard.
And the work of righteousness will be peace; the fruit of righteousness will be quietness and trust forever and ever.
My people will dwell in a habitation of peace, in dwellings safe and secure, and in resting places of untroubled ease.
But hail will flatten the forest, and the city will be brought low to the ground.
Blessed are you who sow beside every stream, who let the ox and the donkey roam free.
